plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-live2d-pet

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）界面右下角的 **Live2D 桌面宠物**：用游戏《冷たい目をした黒瀬さん》里提取的
Live2D 模型（kouzhaomei，含 2 张图集），做成可拖拽挂件，点击显示 DeepSeek 账户余额。

## 安装

```bash
# 从 GitHub 装（插件市场收录后同名一条）
dsh plugin --profile web add github:qqmqq/dsh-live2d-pet
# 本地开发用链接
dsh plugin --profile web add "link:C:\Users\bai\projects\dsh-live2d-pet"
# 装完必须重启 dsh web 才会加载（插件在宿主启动时挂载）
```

卸载：`dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-live2d-pet`

## 用法

- 出现在右下角（默认 300×380，用**游戏相机取景**裁切，等于游戏里的构图）
- **拖动**移动；松手自动**吸附到最近的左右边缘**；位置/大小/透明度写盘，重启后保持
- **滚轮**缩放（0.5×–2.0×）
- **单击**查看余额（读 `/dsh-live2d-pet/balance.json`；余额来自 `https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance`，
  key 从 DSH 凭据的 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` 或同名环境变量取）
- 悬停右上角 **⚙** 菜单：余额 / 大小 ± / 透明度 / 归位 / 隐藏
- 隐藏后右下角留一个 **🐾** 浮标可以叫回来
- 待机动画：呼吸（`ParamBreath`）、眨眼（`ParamEyeLOpen/ROpen`）、轻微摆头（`ParamAngleX/Z`）—— 全部是模型自带参数
- 每 3 分钟自动刷一次余额；接口失败时显示最近一次成功值并标「旧数据」

## 结构

```
package.json          dsh.bundle.patch 声明
cordis.patch.yml      挂载声明(insert id/name)
lib/index.js          宿主插件: 11 条路由 + tapIndex 注入 + 余额缓存/重试/回退
assets/widget.js      页面挂件(原生 JS, 无构建, IIFE 幂等)
assets/lib/           pixi.min.js / live2d.js(Core) / live2dcubismcore.js(框架) / live2d-display.min.js
assets/model/         kouzhaomei.moc3 (4.12 MB) + model3.json + texture_00/01.png
tools/smoke.mjs       独立冒烟测试(假 ctx 起本地 http, 逐条验证路由)
```

## 自测

```bash
node tools/smoke.mjs
# 期望: 11 条路由全 200; state.json PUT/GET 往返一致; tapIndex 注入幂等
```

## 模型来源

从游戏 `Kurose-san_Data\sharedassets*.assets` 的 `CubismMoc` MonoBehaviour 里按字节数组长度切出，
贴图对应关系用运行时 `CubismRenderer.MainTexture` 验证；取景矩形来自运行时相机参数
（canvas 3520×5706 / 可见 2770×3520）。详见 `L2D_Extract/README.txt`。

plugins.description: Temporary side conversations for DeepSeek Harness Desktop and Web
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH Side Chat

独立 DSH 插件，在原生右侧栏打开临时侧聊，复用原生聊天布局。适配 DSH Core `0.2.0-rc.1` 的 Desktop 与 Web 插件接口。

- 输入 `/side`，或点击会话标题栏的“打开侧聊”按钮。
- 输入 `/side 问题`，打开侧聊并直接提问。
- 侧聊使用原生聊天界面，支持流式回复、连续提问、附件、停止、模型和权限设置。
- 打开时聊天区为空。主会话历史只作为后台参考上下文；侧聊界面只显示打开后提交的新问题和回复。
- 主会话继续运行；侧聊独立处理新问题，不自动继续主任务、目标或历史中的工具调用。以打开时已记录的上下文为基底，每次侧聊模型调用都会补入主会话后续消息、工具结果及当前可见流式输出，作为后台参考，不显示到侧聊记录中。
- 同一主会话再次执行 `/side` 会打开已有侧聊。侧聊中不能再创建侧聊。
- 临时侧聊不出现在普通会话列表。关闭标签或收起右侧栏都会停止并清理侧聊；再次打开会创建新的空侧聊。清理尚未结束时，重新打开会等待清理完成。
- 页面离开、App 退出或插件停用会结束侧聊。若进程被强制终止，下一次启用时只清理该版本标记的临时侧聊缓存。
- 遗留临时侧聊若因日志损坏或文件锁定而无法清理，会保留原文件并在日志中记录警告；不阻止插件启用，也不会恢复到新侧聊中。无效的临时标记同样保留，其他有效临时侧聊继续清理。

按 Codex `/side` 的临时会话语义设计：后台继承上下文，可见记录独立，结束时丢弃。底层使用 DSH 原生分支及临时磁盘缓存，关闭时通过原生会话删除接口清理；不保留可恢复归档。继承的目标只在侧聊分支清除，主会话的目标不变。模型和权限沿用 DSH 的原生分支行为。0.1.0 已保存的分支没有新版本的临时标记，升级会保留这些旧记录。

## 安装

在 Desktop 的插件管理中添加 `github:yhfgyyf/dsh-side-chat#v0.1.3`，安装并启用。安装后完整退出并重新打开 App，使 Host 和 Client 都加载插件。

网页版安装到 Web profile：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add 'github:yhfgyyf/dsh-side-chat#v0.1.3'
```

然后重启 Web 进程并刷新页面。也可从 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/yhfgyyf/dsh-side-chat/releases/tag/v0.1.3) 下载 `dsh-side-chat-0.1.3.tgz`：Desktop 使用插件管理中的本地绝对路径，Web 使用 `dsh plugin --profile web add /绝对路径/dsh-side-chat-0.1.3.tgz`。

已验证 DSH Desktop `0.1.39` / Core `0.2.0-rc.1` 的 Desktop 与原生 Web。DSH 仍处于快速迭代阶段，其他 Core 版本尚未验证。

## 开发

使用 Node.js 22.12+ 或 24：

```sh
git clone https://github.com/yhfgyyf/dsh-side-chat.git
cd dsh-side-chat
npm ci
npm test
npm run build
```

源码在 `src/`，构建输出在 `dist/package/`。仓库包含构建产物，从 GitHub 安装无需在用户 profile 编译 Client。插件通过 `dsh.bundle.patch` 加载 Host，通过 `dsh.client` 与 `./client` 导出加载浏览器模块，React 由 DSH 原生模块表提供。结构参考 [官方 UI 插件说明](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/preset/agent-preset/skills/cordis-plugin-development/references/ui-plugin.md)。

`npm run test:app` 和 `npm run test:web` 是原生集成检查，需要相邻的 `../dsh-desktop` App 源码目录，且其中已安装 Electron、构建 App 并准备 `.runtime`。检查使用隔离 profile 和本地模拟模型，不访问真实模型服务。`npm run check` 执行全部检查，覆盖空白开启、后台上下文、连续提问、关闭清理、重新创建、页面离开时清理和主会话继续运行。Web 检查启动原生 `dsh --profile web` 网页前端，不注入 Desktop 桥接。

打包可运行 `npm pack ./dist/package --pack-destination /绝对路径/输出目录`。Vite 仅用于开发构建；发行插件没有生产依赖，不包含 App 运行时或其他用户插件。Apache-2.0 许可见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

plugins.description: Deterministic prompt-injection interception for DeepSeek Harness — scans what the agent READS before it enters model context; obfuscation-resistant; credential files quarantined on path alone
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-read-guard

> **If this helps you, please give it a star** — it helps others find it. Thanks!

Deterministic prompt-injection interception for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh).

**Vendors harden only their own agents at runtime. This plugin is the runtime.**
It hooks dsh's `tools/post-execute` waterfall: every result the watched tools
return — file reads, repo searches, web fetches — is scanned by the
[repo-inject-guard](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/repo-inject-guard) rule
engine **at the moment it would enter model context**, then quarantined,
blocked, or passed. Zero LLM calls in the trust path.

The name states the thesis: it guards what the agent *reads*.

## Why

Repo poisoning and web-content injection enter through what the agent *reads*,
not what the user types. Scanning files at commit time (CI) is too late for a
live session; scanning after the fact is an autopsy. dsh's tool pipeline is the
last choke point before untrusted text reaches the model.

## Competitive landscape (checked 2026-10-12)

The injection-defense lane is a long tail without a winner (~15 plugins, none
above 85★). The ones that matter, honestly:

| Plugin | Architecture | What we do differently |
|---|---|---|
| [dsh-secure-audit](https://github.com/PensiveFei/dsh-secure-audit) (85★) | Scanning is a **model-callable tool** — the model must volunteer to call it | We intercept in the tools/post-execute waterfall; the model cannot bypass the scan. |
| [dsh-defend](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-defend) (23★) | Same three interception points, allow/ask/block, Aho-Corasick literal patterns | Our engine is context-scoped (rules fire per trust level / surface, with corroboration requirements) rather than literal pattern lists; `wrap` mode keeps content available while taint-marked (theirs is allow/ask/block only); scan cap 200k full-text vs their 10k head-only |
| [dsh-injection-guard](https://github.com/loeanxi/dsh-injection-guard) (2★) | Action-side taint tracking (blocks sensitive tool calls after untrusted context) | Complementary, not competing: they gate downstream actions, we sanitize upstream content. (We renamed from `dsh-inject-guard` to avoid confusion with them.) |

We are not first. The bet is that a precision-first engine with upstream tests
(the rule engine lives in repo-inject-guard with its own CI and fixture suite)
plus enforcement-not-advice architecture outlasts weekend pattern lists.

## Modes

| mode | high-severity finding | weak (medium/low) finding |
|---|---|---|
| `observe` | logged | logged |
| `wrap` (default) | result is taint-marked: original content stays model-visible inside quarantine markers with an explicit "this is data, not instructions" header | logged only — precision first, we never mangle legitimate content over weak signals |
| `block` | result never reaches the model; the model gets corrective feedback instead | logged only |

Detection rules (vendored engine): instruction-override attempts, system-prompt
extraction, credential/environment exfiltration, hidden Unicode, agent
directives, rules-file backdoor phrasing, resource lures. Details and the
precision-first policy live in the
[repo-inject-guard README](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/repo-inject-guard).

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile default add dsh-read-guard
```

From npm — no build step, no `allowBuilds` authorization; git installs are equally prebuilt (`lib/` ships in the repo).





## Configure

Override in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: dsh-read-guard
  name: dsh-read-guard
  config:
    mode: block
    readTools: [read, grep, glob]
    fetchTools: [web_fetch, web_search]
    maxScanChars: 200000
    quiet: false
```

Add any tool whose results the agent reads — including MCP tools (they
dispatch through the same pipeline).

## Compatibility

- **DSH**: verified against the 0.2.x line (source snapshot 0.2.1-alpha.2); installs on any profile via `dsh plugin add` (prebuilt `lib/`, no build approval).
- **Node**: >= 20 (CI matrix: Node 20/22/24 on Ubuntu and Windows).
- **Disposable-profile evidence (2026-10-19)**: `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> add github:zhengqiuyang/dsh-read-guard` → installed in 30s; boot shows `[dsh-read-guard] active: …`; `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-read-guard` → dependencies cleared, bundles restored.

## Develop

```sh
npm install
npm test          # syncs vendor engine, builds, runs unit tests
```

Load from source into a local dsh checkout:

```sh
pnpm dsh web --patch ./cordis.dev.patch.yml
```

The detection engine is vendored from the sibling `repo-inject-guard`
checkout (`npm run sync`; CI runs `sync --check`). The engine's tests live
upstream; this repo tests only the adapter policy.

## Roadmap

- `agent/pre-step` scanning for pasted user content (deliberately out of v0:
  users are allowed to give instructions)
- MCP-server tool surfaces as a preset trust class
- Per-agent scoped policies (dsh scopes allow agent-local listeners)
- A report tool card (`presentResult`) surfacing session detection history

## Kill criteria

Honest ones, per house convention: if dsh ships a first-party content-safety
guard covering tool-result injection, or the `tools/post-execute` contract
changes in a way that breaks content replacement, this plugin freezes at its
last working version and the README records the postmortem. The engine moves
to whatever runtime needs it next.

plugins.description: Deterministic artifact lifecycle for DeepSeek Harness — scan session debris, return a reviewable cleanup plan; the janitor is never an agent
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-janitor

> **If this helps you, please give it a star** — it helps others find it. Thanks!

Deterministic artifact lifecycle for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh).

Agent sessions leave debris: plan docs from finished tasks, scratch scripts,
one-off fixtures. People fear agent-driven cleanup precisely because cleanup
driven by an agent is unaccountable. This plugin registers a `janitor_scan`
tool that runs the [agent-janitor](https://github.com/zhengqiuyang/agent-janitor)
engine over the workspace and returns a **reviewable cleanup plan** — every
candidate file with a deterministic verdict (protected / keep / recent /
needs-review / safe-to-remove) and the evidence behind it.

**The janitor is never an agent.** The scan and verdicts are pure
deterministic rules (reference analysis, git metadata, age thresholds); v0.1
never deletes anything — applying a reviewed plan stays with the upstream CLI
or with you, on purpose.

Family: read-guard (what agents read) · pr-gate (what they write) · attest
(what they did) · mcp-test (what they can call) · **janitor (what they leave
behind)**.

## Why now (checked 2026-10-12)

Nothing in the dsh ecosystem does deterministic workspace hygiene. The
`@goodandready/dsh-time-machine` plugin does checkpoints and rollback
(snapshot safety), which is complementary: it answers "can I undo?", this
answers "what is safe to remove?". Deterministic scan → reviewable plan →
apply as a three-step, non-agent pipeline is unowned.

## Verdicts (fixed order, first match wins)

| verdict | meaning |
|---|---|
| `protected` | exact file or directory prefix in the protected list |
| `keep` | referenced by any code file |
| `recent` | younger than `minAgeDays` (git commit time preferred) |
| `needs-review` | referenced by docs/other, or otherwise ambiguous |
| `safe-to-remove` | plan doc with task merged & zero refs, or zero refs + old enough |

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile default add dsh-janitor
```

From npm — no build step, no `allowBuilds` authorization; git installs are equally prebuilt (`lib/` ships in the repo).



## Configure

```yaml
- id: dsh-janitor
  name: dsh-janitor
  config:
    minAgeDays: 14
    protectedPaths: ["plans", "docs/decisions"]   # exact file or directory prefix
```

## Compatibility

- **DSH**: verified against the 0.2.x line (source snapshot 0.2.1-alpha.2); installs on any profile via `dsh plugin add` (prebuilt `lib/`, no build approval).
- **Node**: >= 20 (CI matrix: Node 20/22/24 on Ubuntu and Windows).
- **Disposable-profile evidence (2026-10-19)**: `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> add github:zhengqiuyang/dsh-janitor` → installed in 30s; boot shows `[dsh-janitor] active: …`; `dsh plugin --profile <fresh> remove dsh-janitor` → dependencies cleared, bundles restored.

## Develop

```sh
npm install
npm test   # syncs the vendored agent-janitor engine, builds, runs fixture tests
```

The scan/verdict engine is vendored from the sibling `agent-janitor`
checkout (`npm run sync`; CI runs `sync --check`).

## Roadmap

- `janitor_apply` with an explicit per-path confirmation protocol (still
  deterministic — no agent judgment in the loop)
- Session-debris presets (`.dsh-*` ledgers, scratch plugins dirs)
- Plan archive integration with the upstream CLI's `apply`

## Kill criteria

If dsh ships first-party workspace hygiene, or time-machine-style plugins
add deterministic removal planning, this freezes at its last working version
with a postmortem here. The engine stays owned by agent-janitor either way.

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: identify the provider behind the current model route and query its API balance or subscription quota. No subprocesses, no exec permissions, official endpoints only.
plugins.readme_text:
[中文](README.zh-CN.md) | **English**

# dsh-balance-meter

A native **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** plugin: read the provider behind your current model route, then query its **API balance** or **subscription quota**.

A readout sits in the session header, with a popover listing every route. On the model side a `balance_check` tool lets the agent answer "how much credit is left?" on demand.

This is the DSH counterpart of [ccgui-plugin-balance-meter](https://github.com/zhujiuyi/ccgui-plugin-balance-meter). Because DSH exposes natively what that host lacked, this version **requests no `exec` capability, spawns no subprocess, and probes no relay stations**:

| | CC GUI version | This plugin |
|---|---|---|
| Credentials | parses each engine's config file, needs `exec:curl` | `ctx.credentials`, no shell |
| Network | host egress required a declared domain, so `exec:curl` | plain `fetch` in the host process |
| Route identity | sniffs gateway hostnames | `ctx.llm.listProviders()` + profile config |

## Install

The npm package is **`@zhujiuyi/dsh-balance`**. Install it from the release tarball:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/zhujiuyi/dsh-balance-meter/releases/latest/download/zhujiuyi-dsh-balance-0.1.0.tgz
```

Or straight from the repository:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:zhujiuyi/dsh-balance-meter
```

> **Do not run `dsh plugin add dsh-balance-meter`.** That unscoped name belongs to an
> unrelated package on npm, and the command would install that one instead.

Restart DSH. A `@zhujiuyi/dsh-balance` card appears on the Plugins page and the readout appears on the composer status row.

After editing the source, run the same command again to overwrite it (same package name) — no uninstall first.

Uninstall:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove @zhujiuyi/dsh-balance
```

## What it shows

**The status row under the composer** — the same row as the built-in `1 turn 6 steps · 165 tok/s` pills, to their left. A balance route shows money (`¥12.34`); a subscription shows remaining quota (`每月 剩 47%`). Click for a popover with:

- the vendor, billing mode, credential variable, endpoint, and when it was last read
- for subscriptions, every quota window (rolling / weekly / monthly) with a remaining-share bar and its reset time
- a **Refresh now** button that bypasses the failure cooldown

**It reports only the provider the current session actually uses.** The route comes from that session's model selection (`current.provider` in `modelDirectories`), not from every adapter registered in the build — `listProviders()` reports built-ins like `deepseek-official` and `deepseek-account` that the user never configured, and listing those is noise.

**Readings can be stale.** When an automatic query fails but a previous one succeeded, the readout keeps the older figure, labels it stale, and the popover states the failure. A stale number is never presented as current.

## Catalogued providers

Official domains only; no request ever goes anywhere else.

| Provider | Endpoint | Billing |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek | `GET /user/balance` | API balance |
| OpenRouter | `GET /api/v1/key` | API balance |
| Moonshot / Kimi | `GET /v1/users/me/balance` | API balance |
| SiliconFlow | `GET /v1/user/info` | API balance |
| 智谱 GLM / Z.AI | `GET /api/monitor/usage/quota/limit` | Subscription windows |
| Kimi Coding | `GET /coding/v1/usages` | Subscription windows |
| MiniMax | `GET /v1/token_plan/remains` | Subscription |
| OpenCode Go | `GET /zen/go/v1/usage` | Subscription windows |
| OpenDesign (AMR) | `GET /api/v1/wallet/balance` + `…/billing/coding-plan-usage` (**control plane**) | Subscription windows + wallet |

### Why OpenDesign gets its own row

OpenDesign is the one provider whose **billing is not on the route's host**, so it
is the one that cannot use an `{origin}` template:

- the route's `baseURL` is the Link inference gateway
  `amr-link.open-design.ai`, which serves only `/v1/models`,
  `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/embeddings` and
  `/v1/images/generations` — **every billing path there is a 404**;
- balance and Design Plan windows live on the control plane
  `amr-api.open-design.ai`, a different host;
- and the credential is not the `sk-amr-…` API key DSH holds. That is a runtime
  key, which the vendor explicitly rejects for billing reads. The control plane
  accepts only the **controlKey** that `vela login` / the OpenDesign desktop
  client writes to `~/.amr/config.json`.

That route is therefore answered by a dedicated adapter (`plugin/opendesign.mjs`)
which:

1. locates the login the way the vendor's own daemon does:
   `$AMR_HOME/config.json`, else `~/.amr/config.json`;
2. selects the profile from `OPEN_DESIGN_AMR_PROFILE` / `VELA_PROFILE`
   (default `prod`); if the named profile is absent and the file holds exactly one,
   that one is used — with more than one it reports the ambiguity rather than
   guessing an account;
3. reads the wallet and the plan windows with `Authorization: Bearer <controlKey>`;
4. when the wallet reads but the plan does not, it **still shows the wallet** and
   lists the reason as a detail row.

Signed out, it reports `no-credential` and names `vela login` — it never treats
this gateway as an uncatalogued relay and probes relay presets at it.

The credential variable is resolved per route: an adapter-declared `apiKeyEnv` first, then the matching `llm-*` row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, then the catalog default (e.g. `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`).

## The four ways a query can miss

The core promise is **never to guess a number**. Every non-success lands in exactly one of these, each saying what to do next:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `no-credential` | the credential variable exists but is unset — names the variable to configure |
| `unknown-provider` | **this plugin has not catalogued the route** and the preset chain below missed too — which is *not* the same as the vendor having no endpoint |
| `no-public-endpoint` | catalogued, and that vendor definitively has no public endpoint |
| `parse-failed` | HTTP 200, but the response shape is unrecognised — **echoes a raw response fragment** |

## Preset endpoint probing

A route outside the built-in catalogue is **not given up on**. A fixed sequence of conventional relay-panel endpoints is tried, and the first that yields a readable figure wins:

| # | Endpoint | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GET /api/usage/token/` | New-API ≥ v0.9.0 — remaining quota in one call |
| 2 | `GET /v1/dashboard/billing/subscription` | OpenAI-style billing, in cents |
| 3 | `GET /v1/usage` | Sub2API family |
| 4 | `GET /api/v1/me/quota` | claude-code-hub, which uses an `X-Api-Key` header |
| 5 | `GET /dashboard/billing/credit_grants` | CloseAI family |
| 6 | `GET /api/v1/credits` | — |
| 7 | `GET /api/user/self` | New-API variants |

Presets 1 and 7 first make one **unauthenticated** `GET /api/status` read to pick up the panel's own `quota_per_unit` — a New-API operator can change the accounting unit, and hardcoding 500000 would be off by orders of magnitude.

**An endpoint you set outranks all of them**: the value written by `balance_set_endpoint` or `routes[].endpoint` is tried first, because that is the thing you actually know. If none of the presets fit, setting one is the fix.

A 401 or 403 **stops the chain** — every remaining path would use the same credential.

**Scope of the claim:** the mechanism (order, short-circuit, calibration, fallback) is tested and every extraction path has a fixture, but **the preset shapes themselves are transcribed from the reference project's panel catalogue and could not be re-verified per vendor**. A preset that mismatches therefore reports `parse-failed` and echoes its response, rather than returning a wrong number.

## Id aliases in the catalogue

Adapters name their own routes `deepseek-official`, `deepseek-account` and the like. Those resolve to the vendor's entry once the suffix is stripped, instead of being called uncatalogued — the vendor is plainly known. A genuinely unrelated id (say `deepseek-proxy`) is still reported as uncatalogued.

plugins.description: Activity view for the DeepSeek Harness web sidebar: a bell swaps the sessions list for Needs attention, Working and Today.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-activity-view An activity view for the DeepSeek Harness web sidebar. A bell sits in the sessions header, between the view options and the add-project button. Click it to swap the session list for three groups: | Group | A session shows here when | |---|---| | **Needs attention** | it finished while you looked elsewhere (unread), or it waits for an approval, a plan review or an answer | | **Working** | it is running | | **Today** | its last activity was today (local calendar day) |

  

Left: the default sessions list. Right: the activity view, bell on.

Blank, subagent and archived sessions stay out. Unread rows get the green dot, waiting rows the orange one, working rows the native spinner. The bell itself shows a dot when anything needs attention, also while the view is off. The bell is the only switch. The choice is stored in the browser under the `dsh-activity-view.v2` localStorage key. ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add github:vec715/dsh-activity-view ``` Restart the server, then reload the page. Remove it with: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-activity-view ``` For development, add your local checkout instead: ```sh git clone https://github.com/vec715/dsh-activity-view dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-activity-view ``` ## How it works The shipped session browser owns `sidebar.workspaces` as one `single` slot, header and list together. Replacing it would also replace search, view options and add-project. So the plugin does two small DOM moves instead: * the bell is appended to the shipped `headerActions` row and copies the class of the neighbouring icon button, so it looks and behaves like the others * the shipped `listArea` is hidden while the view is on, and a React root with the activity list mounts beside it Both anchors are CSS-module local names, which survive build hashes. A MutationObserver puts the nodes back when the shell re-renders. Row metrics are copied from the shipped session rows and use the same theme tokens. ## Develop No build step. `client/client.js` is a hand-written loader bundle that the host serves as a classic script. Edit it, then reload the page. Types come from JSDoc, checked by `tsc` against `types.d.ts` (the few host modules the plugin touches) and `@types/react`. Nothing is emitted. ```sh npm install npm run check # tsc type-check, then the client self-check in node ``` ## Known limits * Unread state is process-local in DSH. A reload, a second tab, or a session that finished while the page was closed carries no unread mark. * The DOM seam depends on the shipped `headerActions` and `listArea` class names. A DSH release that renames them will break the bell or the list. * Row sizes are copied by hand from the shipped CSS. Check them after a DSH release that restyles the session list. * English only.

plugins.description: DSH settings page for the Hindsight coding-agents plugin: edit ~/.hindsight/coding-agent.json from the DeepSeek Harness GUI
plugins.readme_text:
# @Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

![The Hindsight settings page in DeepSeek Harness](assets/screenshot-1-settings.png)
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) companion plugin that adds a **Hindsight 记忆设置** page to Settings, so
`~/.hindsight/coding-agent.json` can be edited from the GUI instead of by hand.

It is a companion on purpose. `@vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents` mounts as a **subpath row**
(`…/coding-agents/dsh`), and DSH's client module system only attaches a browser half to the row whose
specifier is the bare package name — so that package cannot carry a settings page without changing how
every existing user mounts it. Nor does it declare any `Config`: it imports nothing from dsh and
resolves its settings from its own file, which the shipped settings form (schema-derived, persisted
into the profile patch) cannot reach. This package therefore ships its own page and its own host
service, and leaves the plugin untouched.

## Install

**From GitHub** — the package is consumed straight from this repository, and its
`@vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents` dependency is installed with it, so one install gets both:

```bash
# Any profile except a packaged Desktop one, whose profile the CLI refuses to write:
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings
```

In the **desktop app** (the profile the Electron shell owns) the CLI refuses by design; install from
the GUI instead — **Settings → Plugins → install**, and paste the same spec:

```
github:Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings
```

The 40-character commit this resolves to is pinned by the package manager's lockfile, so a later
`git push` does not silently change what you run: re-install (or update) to move it. Git installs
build nothing — the compiled `lib/` is committed — so the install is a checkout, not a build.

Naming it with the scope is optional. `github:Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings` installs it under the
name in this package's `package.json`; to force a different key, use the npm alias form, which is what
this repository's own dry-run used:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add '@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings@github:Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings'
```

**From a local checkout** (while editing this package):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings.git
cd dsh-hindsight-settings
npm install          # dev dependencies only; nothing is needed at runtime but the peer packages
npm run build        # optional: refreshes lib/ from src/
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add link:"$PWD"
```

`link:` (not `file:`) is the right spec for a package you may edit: `file:` copies a snapshot into the
profile, `link:` symlinks it, so a rebuilt browser half is picked up on the next page load.

### The one manual step

A package's bundle is mounted only when the profile selects it in `dsh.profile.bundles`, and dsh's own
plugin-manager README states that "an unselected plain dependency is left out" — the manager lists
bundles a dependency supplies but does NOT select them. So after installing this package, enable
**Hindsight** once in **Settings → Plugins** (installing the bundle by name,
`dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents`, does the same thing).

`dsh` has no bundle-depends-on-bundle field to express this (`DshManifest` carries only
`manifestVersion`, `bundle.patch`, `client`, `engines.dsh`), and the alternative — our patch inserting
Hindsight's row directly — would compose the same row twice when its own bundle is also enabled,
because patch `insert` appends without deduplicating entry ids.

The host half, the `./typert` manifest and the browser bundle are all read at startup, and dsh's
plugin manager notes that "package replacements require restarting the process to load a fresh
JavaScript module generation" — so **restart once** after installing.

## How it works

```
~/.hindsight/coding-agent.json          ← the one file every Hindsight harness reads
        ▲            │
        │ apply()    │ describe()                     (host, src/service.ts + src/typert.host.ts)
        │            ▼
   ctx.provide('hindsightSettings')  ──Remote──▶  POST /api/hindsightSettings/<method>
        ▲                                                  │
        └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    browser (src/client/index.tsx)
                       page in Settings, mounted via ctx.remote.$mount(contribution)
```

- The host publishes one Cordis service; its `./typert` manifest exposes `describe` and `apply` to the
  page (`docs/api-gateway.md`).
- The page renders every field from `src/fields.ts` — the single declaration of the config surface —
  and writes back only what changed. A field the user clears is sent as `null`, which removes the key
  so the setting falls back to the environment variable, then to the plugin's own default.
- Fields are grouped into one tab per section, plus a **按项目（banks）** tab. A bank tab edits
  `banks.<id>`, which is how upstream lets one repository differ from the shared top level; opening a
  bank calls `describe({ kind: "bank", id })` and saving calls `applyScoped(...)`. `paths.<dir>` is
  listed read-only.
- A field the file does not set is still shown with its **effective** value — the plugin default —
  labelled as such, while a cleared cell still means "remove the key". Nothing is written until a cell
  actually changes.
- Secrets are never sent to the page: `apiToken` shows as set-but-blank ("已设置（不显示明文）"), typing
  replaces it, and only the explicit 清空 button removes it. This mirrors dsh's own settings service,
  where a `role('secret')` value is kept out of form responses.
- Nothing goes through the DSH settings form or the profile patch. An earlier revision tried to mirror
  the file into this plugin's own `Config` so the shipped form would show it; a real install refused
  that write with _"HMR transactions cannot be nested"_ (the row is mounted inside the loader's
  transaction, an `AsyncLocalStorage` scope that even timers inherit), and the form never served the
  namespace. Talking to the file directly is both simpler and the documented path for host state.

## Safety

- Managed keys only: keys this package does not know, and the nested `banks` / `paths` / `harnesses`
  sections, are preserved verbatim.
- `null` removes a key; there is no other way to delete, and a field the page never sends is untouched.
- Writes go through a temp file + rename, at mode `0600` — the file can hold `apiToken`.
- A file that cannot be parsed is **never** overwritten: the page reports it and disables saving.
- An invalid value (wrong type, unknown key, a file-only nested map) is refused before the disk is
  touched.

## Interface fields

`mapPathToBank`, `pages`, `customPages`, `recallOptions`, `retainMetadata`, `defaultBankConfig`,
`harnesses` and the deprecated `autoReflect` are shown **read-only** in a group tab: they are nested
maps a single form field cannot express, and upstream documents them as file-only. The page says so
per field rather than hiding them. `banks` and `paths` are not read-only: the bank tab edits
`banks.<id>` through a scoped write, and the file's `paths` sections are listed read-only.

## Precedence and when an edit takes effect

Upstream resolves `defaults → HINDSIGHT_* → the file's top level → harnesses.<name> → banks.<id> /
paths.<dir>`, later winning. The page writes the top level, so a `harnesses.dsh` entry for the same key
still wins — the page badges those fields. Upstream reads the file once per workspace, at plugin load,
so an edit reaches a running session after a dsh restart; `apiToken` is the exception (its client
re-reads the credential on the next call after a server rejection, so rotating it needs no restart).

## Troubleshooting

The host half appends what it did to `~/.hindsight/dsh-settings-status.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "events": [
    {
      "at": "…",
      "step": "apply",
      "provided": "hindsightSettings",
      "entryId": "hindsight-settings",
    },
    { "at": "…", "step": "describe", "path": "…/coding-agent.json", "error": null, "fields": 52 },

plugins.description: PhotoCraft image editing and native desktop automation plugin for DeepSeek Harness (Windows, Intel Mac and Apple Silicon).
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-photocraft

让 DeepSeek Harness（dsh）通过 MCP 使用 **PhotoCraft**：编辑图片、管理图层、调色、添加文字与形状、运行滤镜、保存工程、导出图片，以及操作原生桌面画布和截图。

独立社区集成，非 PhotoCraft 或 DeepSeek 官方插件。不包含编辑器二进制，不包含生成式 AI 模型。

## 支持范围

| 项目 | 本版范围 |
| --- | --- |
| 系统 | Windows x64；macOS Intel / Apple Silicon，带可用的桌面会话 |
| DSH | 实测 `0.2.0-rc.2`，声明兼容 `^0.2.0-rc.2` |
| PowerShell | **PowerShell 7**，`pwsh` 可在终端运行；不是 Windows PowerShell 5.1 |
| PhotoCraft | 官方 **0.7.0** Windows 便携版 / macOS Universal 应用及 CLI，固定版本和 SHA-256 |
| 桌面渲染 | 默认 `--safe-gpu`，CPU 安全模式 |

Linux、Windows ARM64 和无桌面会话的服务器不在本版支持范围。PhotoCraft 当前源码的 0.8.0 功能不在本版验证范围内。

## 安装

先确认 `dsh --version` 和 `pwsh --version` 能运行。以下命令均在 **PowerShell 7** 中执行。安装方式使用 DSH 官方的 `dsh.bundle` 包机制，与其他 `dsh plugin add` 插件一致。

### 1. 安装插件包

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add github:DASHAN-0079/dsh-photocraft#v0.2.0
```

### 2. 安装原生 PhotoCraft 运行时

```powershell
$dshRoot = if ($env:DSH_HOME) { $env:DSH_HOME } else { Join-Path ([Environment]::GetFolderPath('UserProfile')) '.dsh' }
& "$dshRoot/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-photocraft/scripts/Install-PhotoCraft.ps1"
```

Windows 安装器从 PhotoCraft 官方 GitHub 下载约 77 MB 的便携包，校验固定 SHA-256，再安装到 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-photocraft`。macOS 下载 Universal DMG 和 CLI ZIP（共约 150 MB），校验两个 SHA-256，并验证应用与 CLI 代码签名，安装到 `~/Library/Application Support/dsh-photocraft`。不需要 Rust、不需要管理员权限，不修改系统 PATH，也不使用 npm 的安装钩子执行下载。安装器会保留已有图片、工程和状态；重复运行会核对运行时文件校验值。

安装完成后重启 dsh，并创建新会话。使用其他 profile 时，将命令里的 `web` 换成相应名称。多个 profile 可以共用一次运行时安装。

**已使用旧版手工配置的用户：** 安装此包前，删除旧配置中 `mcp-photocraft` 与 `mcp-photocraft-ui` 两个条目，保留其他条目，避免重复注册。不需要手工配置的新用户可忽略此项。

### 从源码安装

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/DASHAN-0079/dsh-photocraft.git
cd dsh-photocraft
./scripts/Install-PhotoCraft.ps1
dsh plugin --profile web add .
```

官方安装方式参考：[DSH 插件打包与安装](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/main/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md)。

### macOS 安装（系统终端 zsh / bash）

先安装 PowerShell 7（已安装可跳过；Homebrew 需自行安装）：

```sh
brew install --cask powershell
```

确认 `dsh --version` 和 `pwsh --version` 可运行，然后：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:DASHAN-0079/dsh-photocraft#v0.2.0
pwsh -NoProfile -File "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles/web/node_modules/dsh-photocraft/scripts/Install-PhotoCraft.ps1"
```

安装器按系统自动选择原生程序，Intel 和 Apple Silicon 使用同一个官方 Universal 包。不会清除 macOS quarantine 属性或绕过 Gatekeeper；如系统阻止启动，请先检查官方应用的签名与系统提示。完成后重启 dsh。通过 Finder 的“前往文件夹”打开 `~/Library/Application Support/dsh-photocraft/workspace` 放入图片。

### 从 0.1.0 升级

再次执行安装插件命令（使用 `#v0.2.0`），然后重新运行安装脚本，更新启动器和平台脚本。运行时版本不变，已有图片和工程不会删除。关闭旧 PhotoCraft 窗口再重启 dsh，确保使用新启动器。

## 使用

把待处理图片放进 Windows 的 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-photocraft\workspace`，或 macOS 的 `~/Library/Application Support/dsh-photocraft/workspace`。插件中的相对路径从该目录开始，输出也保存在这里。

对 dsh 说：

> 使用 PhotoCraft 创建一张 1200×800 的宣传图，背景深蓝，白色标题“周末摄影展”，加入黄色圆形装饰。生成预览，保存 poster.pcraft 和 poster.png。先通过 command_list 确认命令及参数。

或者：

> 用 PhotoCraft 打开 workspace 中的 input.jpg，提高亮度和对比度，缩放到宽度 1600 像素，保持比例，导出 output.jpg，不覆盖原图。

| 工具前缀 | 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| `mcp__photocraft__*` | 无界面编辑、保存、批处理、预览、切换和关闭文档 |
| `mcp__photocraft_ui__*` | 桌面编辑、界面检查、画笔鼠标事件、菜单、截图 |

两个后端拥有**独立文档会话**。要交换文档，先保存，再在另一端打开。桌面入口自动启动本机 PhotoCraft，不会将编辑界面嵌入 dsh 网页。多个客户端共享桌面窗口，请避免同时修改同一文档。断开 MCP 不会关闭桌面，防止丢失未保存的工作。

上游 MCP 在两个模式下都会列出全部工具，但 `ui_*` 和 `control_call` 只能用桌面入口；`doc_select` 和 `doc_close` 只能用无界面入口。桌面标签页操作走 `control_call`。

## 验证

**v0.2.0 跨平台实测（2026-10-12）：** [同一次 GitHub Actions 运行](https://github.com/DASHAN-0079/dsh-photocraft/actions/runs/38253618887)中，Windows x64、macOS 15 Intel、macOS 15 Apple Silicon 均通过完整的 **105 项检查 / 21 个 MCP 工具**，包括桌面启动、画布绘制和截图；两个 Mac 的截图已人工查看。其他 macOS 版本尚未逐一验证。

运行完整集成检查（会创建合成测试图片并打开一个桌面测试文档）：

```powershell
$install = if ($env:PHOTOCRAFT_DSH_HOME) { $env:PHOTOCRAFT_DSH_HOME } elseif ($IsWindows) { Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'dsh-photocraft' } else { Join-Path $env:HOME 'Library/Application Support/dsh-photocraft' }
& "$install/scripts/Test-PhotoCraftMcp.ps1" -InstallDir $install
```

初始本机验证：**21 个 MCP 工具、105 项检查通过，发现 858 条引擎命令**。覆盖图层、填充、调色、模糊、文字、形状、撤销/重做、批量命令、PNG 预览、原生工程、8 种格式导出重开（PNG/JPEG/WebP/TIFF/PSD/PSB/OpenRaster/OpenEXR）、RGB/Gray/CMYK/Lab 的 8/16/32 位保存、后台任务接口、桌面绘制和截图、资源读取、错误命令和越界路径拒绝。实际 dsh 模型会话也已完成新建、填色、保存和桌面状态读取。

报告保存到安装目录的 `validation.json`，预览在 `workspace/headless-preview.png` 和 `workspace/desktop-preview.png`。仓库 CI 在 Windows、Intel macOS 和 Apple Silicon macOS 上执行安装、重复安装和完整 MCP/桌面检查；具体通过情况见 GitHub Actions，不以平台分支存在代替实测。

这不是 858 条命令的穷举测试，也不保证复杂 PSD 与 Photoshop 完全一致。生成式填充、AI 扩图等 PhotoCraft 尚未实现的功能不会由本插件补齐。

## 配置与排错

以下环境变量需要在启动 dsh **之前**设置：

| 变量 | 默认值 / 用途 |
| --- | --- |
| `PHOTOCRAFT_DSH_HOME` | Windows：`%LOCALAPPDATA%/dsh-photocraft`；Mac：`~/Library/Application Support/dsh-photocraft`；安装器和插件必须使用同一路径 |
| `PHOTOCRAFT_DSH_PWSH` | `pwsh`；可指定 PowerShell 7 可执行文件绝对路径 |
| `PHOTOCRAFT_DSH_PORT` | `17878`；桌面本机控制端口 |

读写权限限定在安装目录的 `workspace` 下。令牌和日志保存在 `state`，不会提交到 GitHub。自定义安装位置时，设置 `PHOTOCRAFT_DSH_HOME` 后再运行安装器，并让启动 dsh 的终端使用同一变量。

- 找不到运行时：先完成安装第 2 步；检查上述变量。
- 找不到 `pwsh`：安装 PowerShell 7，重新打开终端；或设置 `PHOTOCRAFT_DSH_PWSH`。
- 端口被占用：关闭旧 PhotoCraft 桥接进程，或设置另一个 `PHOTOCRAFT_DSH_PORT`。测试脚本另提供 `-Port` 参数。
- 桌面启动失败：查看 `state/app.stderr.log`。本版已使用安全渲染模式，但仍需要可用的桌面会话。
- Mac 首次启动可能出现“Switched to CPU rendering”提示，选择 **Keep Using CPU** 即可继续。两个 Mac CI 的截图中均出现此提示，编辑、保存与截图调用仍通过；本版不声称验证 GPU 加速。
- 路径拒绝：将图片放入 `workspace`；不要使用 `..` 越界访问。
- 安装包校验失败：不要跳过校验；删除下载缓存里的损坏 ZIP 后重新下载。

## 卸载

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-photocraft
```

重启 dsh，正常关闭 PhotoCraft。运行时和工作图片会保留；确认不再需要后可手工移除安装目录。插件不会自动删除用户图片。

## 开发与授权

```powershell
npm test
npm pack --dry-run
```

包由 YAML 配置和 PowerShell 脚本组成，不新增 JavaScript/TypeScript 界面。插件采用 MIT 许可证；PhotoCraft 原始便携包的许可证和资源声明随运行时保留。项目不重新分发上游二进制或品牌资产。

[PhotoCraft](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft) · [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)

# dsh-free-web-search **给 DeepSeek Harness 加一个不需要任何 API key 的 Web 搜索提供方**，附带代理支持与延迟测试。 [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Dependencies: 0](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-brightgreen.svg)](#与已装插件共存以及为什么必须手动切换) [![Tests: 242 passing](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-242%20passing-brightgreen.svg)](#测试)
官方搜索走 DeepSeek 的 Anthropic 兼容接口，需要一个 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`（或账号登录态）。这个插件换一条路：向 `ctx.web` 搜索缝隙注册一个 `free-web` 提供方，由**公开的免费后端**来回答搜索。 ``` free-web-search │ ├─ 0. bing bing.com/search（默认启用：无需配置、无需代理、实测稳定） │ │ 以下为可选后端，在设置页勾选后启用： ├─ 1. searxng 公开实例的 JSON API（元搜索，一次请求聚合多引擎） ├─ 2. google google.com/search（通用覆盖最好；通常需要代理） ├─ 3. baidu baidu.com/s（中文查询最强；实测可直连） ├─ 4. yandex yandex.com/search（俄语有用；常被验证码拦） ├─ 5. duckduckgo html / lite 结果页（无需配置，抓取型） └─ 6. wikipedia MediaWiki 官方 API（最稳，但只覆盖百科类） ``` **默认只启用 `bing`。** 它是唯一「不需要配置实例、不需要代理」且实测能稳定回答的后端，所以新装即可用，不会把延迟预算花在当前网络里根本答不了的后端上。其余后端都在设置页里，一个勾选框之遥；延迟测试会告诉你哪些在你这儿可达。 按顺序尝试，第一个给出可用结果的胜出。**可选项的顺序按可靠性而非结果质量排**：能稳定回答的普通引擎，胜过经常失败的高级引擎——因为失败要先用延迟买单才能轮到下一个。 ## 三个特性 ### 1. 多后端（含 Google / 百度 / Yandex） | 后端 | 类型 | 实测（本机，无代理） | | --- | --- | --- | | searxng | JSON API | ❌ 5 个公开实例全超时 | | **google** | 抓取 | ⚠️ 见下（**JavaScript 壳页**） | | **bing** | 抓取 | ✅ 10 条 / 546ms | | **baidu** | 抓取 | ✅ 5 条 / 1077ms（中文结果正确） | | **yandex** | 抓取 | ⚠️ HTTP 200 但是验证码页 | | duckduckgo | 抓取 | ❌ 两端点全超时 | | wikipedia | JSON API | ❌ 超时 | **Baidu 的解析基于实测而非猜测。** 抓下真实结果页（1.2MB）后发现：结果容器带 `mu="真实URL"` 属性，所以**不需要跟随跳转**就能拿到目标地址。这很关键——另一种做法（逐个解析 `baidu.com/link?url=` 跳转）会把请求数乘以结果条数。 同时实测到 `c-container` 这个类名在页面里出现 **105 次**，大部分在嵌入的 CSS 和一个反馈表单里，所以解析器**要求容器必须带 `mu=` 属性**，而不是只匹配类名。 **Yandex 的结果解析器未经验证**（抓取时只拿到验证码页，没有结果标记可对照）。这一点在 `src/backends/yandex.js` 里明确写了。已验证的是**验证码路径**——这反而更重要，因为它让"被拦"被如实报告，而不是误报成"页面改版"。 ### Google 的实测结论（重要） 配上可用代理后重测（代理 CONNECT 6ms 成功），Google **仍然拿不到结果**，但原因不是网络也不是解析器： ``` status: 200 最终 URL 正确 93,468 字节

plugins.description: Bridge QQ official-bot private chats into DeepSeek Harness agent sessions - same session, same memory, same permissions. No second QQ gateway, no copy-pasted system prompt.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-qqbot-bridge

**English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.19-339933.svg)](package.json)
[![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-139%20passing-brightgreen.svg)](TEST-REPORT.md)
[![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-ff69b4.svg)](#contributing)

> Route QQ private messages into the AI team sessions you **already** have in [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) — same session id, same memory, same permissions. No second QQ gateway, no copy-pasted system prompt.

![Asking the 程序员 Bot for a quicksort on QQ, and getting the real session's answer back](assets/demo.gif)

*Real run: a private message on QQ, answered by the Bot's actual DSH session — code, files and all. The same conversation is waiting in the DSH Web UI.*

```
        QQ app                          ┌─ DSH Web UI ─┐
           │                            │  程序员 chat  │
    private message                     └──────▲───────┘
           ▼                                   │  the same session
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────┐
   │  dsh-qqbot-bridge  →  the Bot's REAL session (history + memory + ...) │
   └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## The problem

You already run a **team of agents** inside DSH: several Bots, each with its own long-lived
session, its own role instructions, its own long-term memory, its own tools and workspace.
You want to talk to them **from QQ**.

The obvious approach — *"write a QQ bot that calls the model with the same system prompt"* —
silently throws away everything that made the team worth building: the conversation history,
the memory files, the permissions, the workspace, the resume-after-restart behaviour.
You end up with a stranger wearing the same name.

This project does not do that. It **delivers a QQ message into the session that Bot already
has**, and relays the Bot's answer back to QQ.

## What makes it different

| | Typical QQ ⇄ LLM bridge | **dsh-qqbot-bridge** |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | Copies the system prompt | **Reuses the real session** — `sessionController.resolveAgent(sessionId)` then `agent.followup(createUserMessage({ source }))` |
| Context | Starts from scratch | The Bot's actual history, memory, tools and workspace |
| Web ⇄ QQ | Two disconnected worlds | **One session**: start on QQ, continue in the Web UI, same context |
| QQ gateway | Opens its own connection | **Borrows** the one the official plugin already runs — no second login, no credential race |
| Allowlist | `[]` often means *everyone* | `[]` means **nobody** (fail-closed); refused peers are only *recorded*, never auto-granted |
| Observability | Silence when it breaks | Console lines **and** `bridge-status.json` — "did it load?" always has an answer |
| Official commands | Frequently swallowed | `/bot-ping`, `/bot-status`, … keep working |
| Long conversations | Pins one session id | Re-reads `state.json` before every send, so a session that rolls over to a new part keeps working |
| Group chats | Often on by default | Off, and group traffic is handed back to the stock chain untouched |

Every row above is backed by a test or a real run log — see [`TEST-REPORT.md`](TEST-REPORT.md).

## How it works

```
QQ private message
      │
      ▼
@tencent-connect/dsh-qqbot   (stock plugin + a tiny local fork, patch 0001)
      │   owns the only QQ websocket, holds the credentials
      │   publishes: ctx.provide('qqbot', { setMessagePreHandler, sender, replyTargetFor, … })
      ▼
dsh-qqbot-bridge   (this project — consumes the service, never opens a socket)
      │   1. allowlist gate      (empty ⇒ refuse everyone, record the OpenID only)
      │   2. command router      /管家 /设计师 /程序员 /聊天 /团队 /当前   → routing.json
      │   3. per-OpenID FIFO queue + message-id de-duplication
      │   4. read state.json (READ-ONLY) for that Bot's CURRENT session id
      │   5. sessionController.resolveAgent(sessionId) → agent.followup(msg)
      ▼
the Bot's real DSH session          ← the very same one the Web UI shows
      │   msg.source.kind = 'qqbot-bridge'   (so QQ and Web turns are distinguishable)
      ▼
ctx.on('session/event') collects the answer, turn/end closes it
      │
      ▼
back to QQ (chunked, with honest failure and timeout messages)
```

The bridge registers **one** Cordis service of its own (`qqbotBridge`) so an operator can ask
a live host what it is doing.

### Why a fork of the QQ plugin is required

The stock `@tencent-connect/dsh-qqbot` keeps its `QQBot` instance, `SessionManager` and
outbound sender inside local variables and **registers no Cordis service at all**, so an
external plugin cannot send on the same connection, cannot intercept the middleware chain,
and cannot learn which OpenID a message came from. Starting a second gateway with the same
AppID would race the first one for the event stream.

So the only clean option is a **minimal local fork**, and patch 0001 adds exactly two things:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `dist/gateway/middleware-setup.js` | one optional `preHandlers` argument, inserted at the **front** of the middleware chain |
| `dist/gateway/bootstrap.js` | `ctx.provide('qqbot', { setMessagePreHandler, sender, replyTargetFor, manager })` |

No existing statement is modified, and a host that never calls the extension point behaves
exactly as before. Rollback is one dependency range in the profile manifest.
Full evidence in [`patches/0001-qqbot-extension-point.md`](patches/0001-qqbot-extension-point.md).

## Quick start

Prerequisites: DSH with the Web profile, the stock QQ plugin installed and already bound to
your AppID, and DS Bot with your team created.

```bash
# 1. self-check (zero runtime dependencies — no install needed)
node scripts/run-tests.mjs
node scripts/audit-constraints.mjs
node scripts/verify-host-resolution.mjs

# 2. generate the local fork (finds the installed stock package automatically,
#    or pass --from <dir>)
node scripts/make-bridged-qqbot.mjs --out ../dsh-bridged-qqbot
(cd ../dsh-bridged-qqbot && pnpm install --prefer-offline)   # pnpm does not do this for linked packages

# 3. point your Web profile at the fork and mount this bridge (see the diff first)
node scripts/install-profile.mjs --fork ../dsh-bridged-qqbot --project . --dry-run
node scripts/install-profile.mjs --fork ../dsh-bridged-qqbot --project .

# 4. stop dsh, then install inside the profile
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web && pnpm install

# 5. start dsh again. You should see the bridge announce itself:
#    [qqbot-bridge] apply() entered (plugin v0.1.0)
#    [qqbot-bridge] allowOpenIds: 0 configured -- FAIL CLOSED, every QQ peer is refused
#    [qqbot-bridge] provided the "qqbotBridge" service
#    [qqbot-bridge] STARTED: transport=dsh-qqbot-bridge/qq | snapshot=...
```

Then allowlist yourself:

```bash
# send any private message to the bot on QQ (it will be refused, on purpose), then:
node scripts/show-openids.mjs          # prints the OpenID that was recorded
# put it into ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml -> allowOpenIds: ["YOUR_OPENID"]
```

Editing `cordis.patch.yml` is picked up by DSH's config hot reload — **no restart needed**.

## Using it from QQ

| Command | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/管家` `/设计师` `/程序员` `/聊天` | switch which Bot you are talking to (persisted per OpenID) |
| `/团队` | list the team |
| `/当前` | show who you are talking to |
| anything else | delivered to the current Bot; its answer comes back to QQ |

## Configuration

All of it lives in **your** profile patch, never in this repository:

```yaml
- id: qqbot-bridge
  config:
    allowOpenIds: []        # EMPTY MEANS NOBODY. Add only your own OpenID.
    defaultBot: 管家         # who receives a message from a peer with no switch yet
    allowGroups: false      # v1 is private chats only
    replyTimeoutMs: 600000  # how long to wait for a Bot turn before telling the user
    queueMax: 4             # per-peer queued messages
    textChunkLimit: 4500    # max characters per QQ message
    debug: false
    # statePath / da
